commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finelog] Report relay health and recover newer local catalogs (#9139)

Regional forwarding could stall while pods stayed Ready and the hub
still served queries, leaving operators without an independent freshness
signal. This adds a direct JWT-authenticated relay heartbeat that sends
complete namespace snapshots outside the row path. The hub records
receipt and progress with its own clock; Grafana now pages when a
configured sender or required node-agent namespace is missing, or when
local publication or downstream settlement stops advancing.

Startup recovery could also reject a locally newer catalog when
compaction had replaced objects named by the older remote HEAD. Catalog
revision now selects the winner: a newer local revision is retained and
published as a child of the claimed remote tip, while an equal or older
local state is rebuilt from the selected remote catalog.

The bundled Finelog UI now centers table maintenance: table, storage,
index, segment, and forwarding boundaries. The expensive recent-row
preview and unused dashboard editor are removed.

Regional ingestion remains R2-first. The data relay protocol and
catch-up mechanics are unchanged; idempotent batch delivery and
coalesced cursor checkpoints remain follow-up work in the [Loom
plan](https://loom.oa.dev/s/cqdmle8t).

The fixed source was restart-validated on the Marin hub, then rolled
through marin-dev, cw-rno2a, cw-us-east-02a, and cw-us-east-08a. Each
target reported the expected clean build stamp, zero new restarts, and
healthy ingestion; all regional senders delivered fresh independent
status to the hub. The rollout also confirmed recovery of the
[cw-us-east-08a incident](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/423).

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
Fix GCP token expiry skew and cut redundant RPCs and dead code (#9146)

Four independent changes, one per subproject.

`CloudGcpService` read google.auth's `Credentials.expiry` — a naive
datetime
holding UTC — with `.timestamp()`, which interprets a naive datetime in
the
host's local zone, so the cached-token window was skewed by the host's
UTC
offset. On a US/Pacific host a 1-hour access token was cached for 7.9
hours, so
`_headers` kept serving a token GCP had already stopped honoring and
every call
401'd until the skew elapsed. East of UTC the sign flips and the token
is
re-minted on nearly every request. Only non-UTC hosts are affected,
which
includes developer laptops running iris cluster commands against GCP.

The Zephyr coordinator loop ticks every 0.5s and probed worker-job
liveness on
every tick. Each probe is an uncached `GetJobState` RPC to the Iris
controller,
so every pool cost 7,200 controller calls per hour whether or not it had
work in
flight. The probe now runs at most once every 5s. The first tick still
probes
immediately, and the 120s heartbeat timeout — not this probe — bounds
how long a
dead worker pool can go unnoticed.

`marin.execution.disk_cache` and the `distributed_lock` decorator that
composes
with it lost their last production caller when step caching moved into
`StepRunner` (#3265). Their own test file was the only remaining
importer, so the
module, the decorator, and that test go away together.

`WandbConfig.save_xla_dumps` documented uploading XLA compiler dumps to
W&B, but
the callback that read it was never registered as a training hook, so
the option
silently did nothing while the configuration reference still promised
otherwise.
The option, `wandb_xla_logger`, `save_xla_dumps_to_wandb`, and the
now-unused
`is_wandb_available` are removed along with the stale docs rows. Users
who want
XLA dumps can set `XLA_FLAGS=--xla_dump_to=...` and collect the
directory.

---------

Co-authored-by: Nightshift Scout <nightshift@marin.local>

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[eval] Consume Harbor's trial-error taxonomy (#9109)

Snapshot Harbor’s error taxonomy and pinned Git commit during preflight.
The current taxonomy contains 27 infrastructure, 3 agent, 2 passthrough,
and 3 undecided error names. Agent failures remain score-bearing without
a verifier result, and passthrough errors preserve usable verifier
scores.

Undecided errors are known to Harbor but have no default policy. Marin
leaves them ungraded, counts them against the 90% completion gate, and
retries them after backend recovery. Names absent from all four sets are
recorded as taxonomy drift and reject the evaluation as an
infrastructure failure.

Preserve per-type error counts for scored and unscored trials, and
record the exact Harbor commit SHA with each run so taxonomy provenance
does not depend on package-version bumps.

Design:
https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2b19eac3-7cc3-4931-97b2-a4984df2ece7

Fixes #8147

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[evaldash] Group benchmark variants under one family column (#9112)

Settings of one benchmark now share a leaderboard column. Family
membership is
declared in the launcher's eval registry and written to each run's
`eval.family`; `gsm8k` and `gsm8k-0shot` both use family `gsm8k`.
Records without
a family still parse and remain separate columns. Capped `-smoke`
variants stay
unfamilied because scoring surfaces exclude them.

`/panel` returns each family, its variants, and the variant selected for
the
column. It chooses the variant with the most admitted cells for that
request,
breaking ties by eval name; explicitly requesting one sibling pins it.
The
effective `panel` contains one variant per family and controls coverage,
`complete=1`, and aggregation. `benchmarks` and cells retain every
admitted
variant with its metric, cohort, harness version, and run provenance. A
model
that ran only the selected variant therefore covers the visible panel.
Selection and panel rendering use the same completeness rule.

The panel picker stores its selection locally and passes exact eval
names to
the `/panel` request and Compare route. The selected variants are
preserved in
the panel and Compare URLs. `/meta` lists every known sibling so a
narrowed
panel can restore another variant.

Fixes #8143

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[eval] Derive Harbor agent context limits from the served model (#9105)

Derive Harbor agent input and output limits from the model's serving and
generation configuration. A DeepSeek-V4-Flash evaluation served a
1,048,576-token context and a 393,216-token generation budget, but
Harbor compacted at its default 32,768 input tokens, invalidating the
long-context comparison.

With automatic serving overrides enabled, clamp the model's explicit
context limit to the checkpoint's native window before Harbor preflight
and retain the resolved serving configuration for execution. A policy
limit below the resolved model limit wins; a policy limit above it fails
preflight. This prevents an agent budget from exceeding a server window
that was reduced during serving configuration.

If neither model nor policy specifies a limit, retain Harbor's defaults.
Dry-run output and evaluation records include the resolved agent limits.
The `grug-opencode-id` policy requests 64,512 input tokens against its
matching model's 65,536-token window; the 31 catalog models configured
to serve 32,768 tokens now reject that policy at preflight.

Fixes #8212

After

git push \

  origin refs/tags/main-20260913:refs/heads/main
```

git push \
  --force-with-lease=refs/heads/main:29548fbab663b7ea946546ca7efaa473dab55ba5 \
  origin refs/tags/main-backup/20260913/pre-b669cfdc:refs/heads/main
```

#24](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/pull/24), [vLLM
#61](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/pull/61), and this PR

complete. Do

Stop agent workflows from producing new design, research, plan, logbook,
and
snapshot files in the repository. Replace the overlapping artifact
skills with
one opt-in `research` workflow that writes to an existing issue, PR, W&B
report,
published report, or durable session channel.

Remove the design template and the documentation cleanup workflow that
archived
stale docs into `.agents/projects`. Keep `write-tests` as a concise
trigger that
routes agents to `TESTING.md` and module testing guides without
repeating their
contents. Existing historical project and logbook files remain
available; this
change removes active instructions and the lint rule that recommended
creating
more.

[finelog] Recover stale same-writer HEAD tokens (#9135)

Adopt a newer catalog HEAD owned by the same writer as the next
compare-and-swap base when it differs from the local revision being
published.
The current attempt remains deferred; a later retry rebases the current
local
projection onto the observed HEAD. Different writer epochs and
conflicting
content at one revision remain fencing errors.

On cw-us-east-08a, the Cloudflare R2 object store selected generation
221521 for
`telemetry_v1.node_agent` under the running writer epoch while Finelog's
in-memory selection remained at generation 221520. The local SQLite
catalog
then advanced, so every publication presented the stale token and
regional-to-hub
forwarding stopped at 2026-09-11 10:13:24 UTC. The regression test
reduces this
sequence to cached generation 1, remote generation 2, and local
generation 3;
the first attempt adopts generation 2 and the second publishes
generation 3.

Incident: https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/423
